newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's PPB party takes soft stand on re-election.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's PPB party takes soft stand on re-election.

text.p: The Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB), the main potential foe to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's bid for a second term, opted not to force members in Congress vote against re-election, officials said.

A one-day party convention decided to let PPB lawmakers make up their own minds on the issue, merely recommending that senators and deputies back re-election only for future presidents, state governors and mayors, they said.
"It's only a recommendation," said PPB party president Sen. Espiridiao Amin.
The issue, which threatened to split the right-wing PPB, was brought to a head in the party by out-going Sao Paulo Mayor Paulo Maluf, who is eyeing Cardoso's job.

Observors said Maluf, seeking to boost his own presidential aspirations, until recently had hoped the convention would order members to oppose a constitutional amendment allowing Cardoso to stand for re-election.
But he softened his stance in the face of opposition from within the PPB, one of Brazil's largest political parties.
"This is a defeat for Paulo Maluf," said analyst Ricardo Pedreira of consulting firm Santafe Idea. "He had to go back on what he wanted."

The PPB in the past has been a Cardoso ally in Congress. But it recently has become more hostile to the government line, mainly following the victory of Maluf's hand-picked successor in last month's Sao Paulo mayoral vote and the heating up of the re-election debate.

The party, which is allied to the Liberal Party, holds 97 seats in the 513-member Chamber of Deputies. The government needs two majorities of 308 votes each for the re-election amendment to be approved in the lower house.
